newsitem.title: USA: Police pursue leads in hunt for Cosby son's killer.
newsitem.headline: Police pursue leads in hunt for Cosby son's killer.

text.p: A massive manhunt was under way on Friday to find the killer of comedian Bill Cosby's only son as the coroner's office conducted an autopsy in the search for clues.

A woman who may have seen the Thursday morning attack on 27-year-old Ennis William Cosby while he was changing a flat tire alongside a California freeway was said to be in fear of retaliation by the killer and under police protection.
The woman, whose name was not released, was helping police artists come up with a composite sketch of the gunman. Police said she described the killer as a white man.

The 59-year-old comedian and his family were in seclusion, their whereabouts unknown after they left their Manhattan home late on Thursday. Cosby's publicist, David Brokaw, said they had no plans to fly to Los Angeles and were still "back East." There was speculation they may have gone to the Cosby home in western Massachusetts.
The family also issued a statement appealing to the news media to stop staking out their homes and instead allow them to grieve in private.
"We do not accept people coming to our homes because this is a time we want to ourselves to find solutions to questions in our hearts," the Cosbys said in a statement.

At the spot where he was gunned down in the early hours Thursday, a single bunch of red and yellow flowers had been placed in the dirt by the side of the road. A faint blood stain was visible on the pavement.

A spokesman for the Los Angeles County coroner's office said an autopsy was being carried out on the younger Cosby, who was reportedly shot once in the head. Autopsies are routinely carried out in murder cases, he said.

Investigators believe robbery was the likely motive but when asked about that theory on ABC's "Good Morning America," Los Angeles Police Chief Willie Williams said: "We don't know ... we know what was left and what was taken, if something was taken.
"The vehicle obviously was not taken and the perpetrator was only there for a few moments or a few seconds ... but we don't know what was in his mind at this point in time," he said.
Williams said police had been helped by the public. "We've received several phone calls, with people who may have seen (Cosby) or may have seen something.

"We have detectives working almost 24 hours a day now, examining the scene, looking for physical evidence, trying to learn more about the last 24 or 48 hours of Mr. Ennis Cosby, who he was with, who he made contact (with)," the police chief said.

"We're still working with the witness to try to develop a composite that will be good enough to release," Williams said, referring to a distraught woman seen in television news footage wearing a fur coat and high-heeled shoes at the scene of the killing near the usually busy San Diego Freeway.

The identity of the woman was being protected by police, but the Los Angeles Times cited sources as saying she was a friend of Ennis Cosby's and that he was on the way to meet her when he stopped to change a tire on a remote stretch of road in the fashionable Bel-Air neighbourhood.

Citing a highly placed source, the newspaper said Ennis Cosby had called her on his cellular telephone to come to his aid and shine her car's headlights on his Mercedes convertible while he worked. She may have witnessed part of the attack at that time, police say.
The woman, who was driving a Jaguar, was questioned extensively by investigators.
Police Cmdr. Tim McBride told the Times the woman was "freaking out" at the prospect of being pursued by reporters, fearing that the killer might retaliate against her.

The murder sent shockwaves through Hollywood and sparked an outpouring of sympathy for his father -- one of the entertainment industry's most beloved figures. The taping of his CBS series "Cosby" was put on hold at a New York studio.
The younger Cosby overcame dyslexia to earn a master's degree in special education at Columbia University's Teachers College in 1995 and was studying for his doctorate.
